original.target_description: Study 1: independent-samples t-test comparing estimated age of the ambiguous woman between the youngest and oldest observer groups (18–22 versus 49–68 years).

n.sample_role: Participants in the two mutually exclusive final extreme-age groups in this t-test.
n.exclusions: USA final sample after attention checks, valid demographic responses and estimated woman age older than 18 years; non-USA respondents excluded. Recruitment: 666 overall, 418 USA; final USA sample 393. Middle-age participants excluded from this contrast.

replication.target_description: Study 1: one-tailed independent-samples t-test of estimated ambiguous-figure age, youngest versus oldest 8.94% (22 participants per group); intentionally differs from original 10% to avoid splitting tied ages.

n.sample_role: Participants in the analytic extreme-age comparison (22 per age group)
n.exclusions: 14 of 260 recruited participants excluded following eligibility checks (person and female identification), leaving 246. Extreme-group comparison additionally restricted to youngest/oldest 8.94%.
n.location: p. 4, Results, Primary analyses: replication of original findings, paragraph beginning “In the original paper” (publisher full-text HTML)
n.quote: This resulted in a sample of n = 44 with 22 participants in each age group.

es.location: Results, Primary analyses: replication of original findings (canonical HTML text; PDF pagination unavailable)

p.location: Results, Primary analyses: replication of original findings (canonical HTML text; PDF pagination unavailable)

reported_success.quote: In this study, we replicated the finding that older participants estimate the woman in the figure to be significantly older than young participants do.

notes:
Youngest/oldest contrast matched independently. Replication explicitly selects 8.94% rather than 10% to avoid arbitrarily excluding tied ages. Original p retained exactly as printed. Success refers to age-estimate finding; replication authors reject the original perceptual/social-group explanation.
Completion source review (n_o): Explicit mutually exclusive extreme-age participant groups in the same target test.
Completion source review (es_value_o): Printed Cohen’s d for the youngest/oldest test.
Completion source review (pval_value_o): Printed exact p for the same test as d.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Explicit youngest/oldest comparison; printed Cohen’s d and exact one-tailed p belong to the same t-test.
